name: Arthrogryposis-like hand anomaly-sensorineural deafness syndrome
aliases: Arthrogryposis-like hand anomaly with sensorineural deafness
Hand anomaly and sensorineural hearing loss syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital arthrogryposis-like hand anomalies including camptodactyly and syndactyly
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometric testing
Lack of significant involvement of other organ systems such as cardiovascular or neurological beyond hand and hearing abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital arthrogryposis-like hand anomalies and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by audiometric and orthopedic evaluation; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified

laboratory: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural hearing loss
imaging: X-rays showing camptodactyly and syndactyly of hand bones
MRI may show muscle hypoplasia in hands
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic testing may exclude other syndromes
other: Electromyography may show mild muscle involvement
Clinical orthopedic examination confirms joint contractures

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic facial features including whistling face
More severe joint contractures involving multiple limbs
Presence of oral and craniofacial anomalies
Foot deformities rather than hand anomalies

redFlags: Development of neurological deficits beyond hearing loss
Severe respiratory compromise due to musculoskeletal deformities
references: Orphanet: Arthrogryposis-like hand anomaly-sensorineural deafness syndrome, ORPHA:1144
Smith et al., 2002. Clinical features of arthrogryposis-like hand anomaly with sensorineural deafness. Am J Med Genet.
